weather_reasons: NWS hourly forecast includes thunderstorm potential
Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 220515
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1015 PM MST Fri Aug 21 2026

.UPDATE...06Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- High temperatures reach or exceed 110 degrees nearly every day
  through the next week and will be within a few degrees of daily
  records, while morning lows remain unusually warm. 

- Extreme Heat Warning in effect through next Friday evening with
  daily Major to Extreme HeatRisk.

- Isolated thunderstorms will primarily favor higher terrain areas
  through this weekend, with drier and less favorable conditions
  next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
Extreme heat will be the primary weather hazard through the 
short, and long, term forecast. Latest objective analysis shows a 
599dam high centered near the Four Corners region, with 596-598dam
heights over the local area. Heights of this magnitude are at or 
above the 99th percentile of sounding climatology. So, it is no 
surprise that forecast high temperatures this afternoon, and 
through this weekend, will be within a few degrees of daily 
records, topping out around 110-116 degrees. Morning low 
temperatures will also remain very warm and near daily record warm
lows, in the mid 80s to low 90s, offering little to no relief 
from the daytime heat. This combo will lead to widespread Major 
HeatRisk through the weekend and an Extreme Heat Warning remains 
in effect.

The thunderstorm chances for the lower deserts this afternoon are
not great, due to the warm air aloft and drier air that moved in
aloft as well. However, surface dew point temperatures remain
seasonally elevated, ranging from the mid-50s to mid-60s. This is
contributing to high SBCAPE values early this afternoon, up to and
in excess of 1500 J/kg. This setup was resulting in cu development
over prominent terrain features as of 1 PM MST and strong storms 
were already going over southeast AZ where mesoanalysis was 
showing an uncapped environment. The cap over much of south-
central AZ and points westward, although relatively weak (SBCIN 
between -20 to -40 J/kg) will likely keep convective development 
reserved to the prominent terrain features, like the Table Top 
Mtns, Kofas, and perhaps Pinal Mtns. Instability is also expected 
to decline through the rest of the afternoon as the PBL continues 
to mix out. This will inhibit updraft strength with time. Any 
storm that does go up this afternoon will be capable of producing 
strong to severe wind gusts, due to high DCAPE values up to
1800-2000 J/kg. An outflow may move up into south-central AZ 
later this evening from southeast AZ storms, but it will likely
take a very strong outflow to trigger additional activity in
northwest Pinal and Maricopa Counties.

Guidance shows boundary layer moisture will drop into tomorrow,
with afternoon dew point temperatures across the lower deserts 
mostly in the mid-50s. This will result in lower SBCAPE values,
but surface temperatures will be slightly hotter and hi-res models
show weaker inhibition, if not uncapped, and slightly steeper
mid-level lapse rates. This may support slightly better coverage
of afternoon convection tomorrow versus today, but still focusing
primarily over the prominent terrain features. Strong to locally 
severe wind gusts and blowing dust will be the primary hazard with
any storm tomorrow afternoon, with high DACPE values again. It 
still may take one good outflow or multiple outflows and outflow 
collisions to trigger storms near/in the Phoenix area. 

&&

.LONG TERM /MONDAY THROUGH NEXT FRIDAY/... 

Model uncertainty remains for the first half of next week,
primarily with respect to thunderstorm chances, as the position 
of the high is likely to set up somewhere over eastern New Mexico 
and western Texas by Monday. There is good global ensemble 
consensus in a brief increase in moisture and instability Sunday 
evening into Monday, most notably across southwest AZ and 
southeast CA, but NBM forecast PoPs are mostly under 15% for the 
lower deserts both days. At this point, we could continue to see 
mostly slight chances favoring the high terrain into early next 
week, but if moisture does eventually improve enough storm chances
are likely to be higher than what the NBM is depicting. By 
Tuesday, drier air will filter back into the region as the 
subtropical high begins to retrograde back over our region. This 
will limit low end rain chances almost exclusively to the higher 
terrain areas with the lower deserts remaining dry. By the latter 
half of next week, the NBM shows PoPs being confined to the 
Mogollon Rim with no chances for our CWA. 

Temperatures are expected to continue to be more influenced by the 
strong subtropical high as H5 heights hover between 593-596dm across 
the Desert Southwest through early next week. Daytime highs are not 
expected to change much from Sunday to Monday, barring any 
significant change with the convective chances. As mentioned above, 
by Tuesday the subtropical high will start to retrograde back to the 
west and the center will eventually settle over AZ/NM during the 
latter half of the workweek. The high is also expected to 
strengthen to around 596-598dam during this time. The combination
of the center settling over our region and strengthening will 
result in temperatures heating up to around 10 degrees above 
normal for this time of year. Afternoon highs (morning lows) ware
forecast in the 110-116 (85-95) degree range across the lower 
deserts and in the 100-110 (75-85) degree range across the higher 
terrain areas. The increase in temperatures will also result in an
increase in HeatRisk, with widespread Extreme HeatRisk forecast
for the majority of the CWA by Wednesday. There is high confidence
already in the heat forecast for next week. So, the Extreme Heat 
Warning was been extended through next Friday and will likely need
to be expanded to more areas by the middle of the week.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0515Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major aviation concerns are expected through early Saturday
afternoon under SCT to sometimes BKN cloud decks. Winds will
follow familiar diurnal trends with periods of VRB conditions
during the overnight hours. Forecast confidence decreases for late
Saturday afternoon into the evening timeframe. There is a signal
that VCSH/VCTS will initiate as early as 23Z, though rain chances
are only around 20% at this time. To reflect convective
uncertainty, PROB30 groups have been added to each metro 
terminal. If storms do develop, they could provide multiple 
outflows, resulting in gusty and erratic winds, and depending on 
where the outflow originate, BLDU could also become a operational 
factor. Changes in subsequent TAF updates should be anticipated.


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major aviation concerns are expected through the front half of
the TAF period. Winds will favor a westerly component at KIPL,
while VRB conditions will be common at KBLH through Saturday
morning. Forecast confidence decreases as we transition into the
afternoon timeframe due to uncertainty of convective activity.
VCTS have been hinted at for KIPL, but rain chances currently
stand at <10%. This TS signal has been consistent for the past
several hours, so as to not completely ignore the potential, a
PROB30 group has been added to the TAF. Gusty
westerly/southwesterly winds and brief reductions in VIS will be
the main concerns with any storms that come to fruition. 
Convection looks as if it will remain outside the vicinity of 
KBLH, but any changes in forecast guidance may yield the addition 
of a PROB30 or VCTS into that TAF as well.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Hot and seasonally dry conditions are expected nearly every day, 
through next week. Aside from a brief increase in moisture Sunday-
Monday, minimum RH values each afternoon will be around 12-18% 
(15-25% Sun-Mon). Temperatures will range 5-10 degrees above 
normal through the next week, with lower desert highs eclipsing 
110 degrees most afternoons. There will be slight chances for 
storms each afternoon through this weekend, but mostly favoring 
higher terrain areas. Drier conditions, with lower storm chances 
are expected by the middle of next week. Outside of thunderstorm 
outflow winds, winds will follow the typical diurnal tendencies 
with some modest afternoon upslope gustiness.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Record highs:

Date       Phoenix         Yuma         El Centro
----       -------         ----         ---------
Aug 21   114 in 2019    115 in 1969    117 in 1969
Aug 22   113 in 2011    115 in 1969    117 in 1969
Aug 23   114 in 2011    115 in 2011    116 in 1969
Aug 24   115 in 2020    119 in 1985    117 in 1985
Aug 25   113 in 2011    116 in 1962    117 in 1962
Aug 26   117 in 2011    115 in 2020    115 in 1981
Aug 27   114 in 2023    120 in 1981    117 in 1981
Aug 28   117 in 2023    118 in 2023    117 in 2009

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Friday for AZZ530>555-559-
     560.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Friday for CAZ562-565>567-
     569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...Berislavich/Benedict
